title: Sakina and the Unlit Lantern
logline: Sakina tries to give light to Layla and learns you can only share a flame you carry.
story: Layla, who was observer of unseen currents, lived in fear of the dark, and Sakina, who carried stillness, arrived with a grand offer of light. But Sakina's own lantern was cold, kept only for show. However many times Sakina pressed the dead lamp into Layla's hands, no warmth would pass. Only when Sakina stopped to kindle a true flame within did the smallest glow leap, at last, from one wick to the other. Sakina learned that light is never given from an empty hand.
moral: You cannot give a light you have not first kindled within yourself.
